evidence: Cic. N.D. 2.26: externus et adventīcius tepor (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Ac. 2.4: illa externa, “outward goods” (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: What comes from outside or belongs to the outside; with regard to one’s family or country it is foreign, as of an enemy from abroad (Cic. Cat. 2.29) (Lewis & Short).
The outer of two: the outer wall, the outer side; the opposite of interior.

phrases.latin: nōs autem illa externa cum multīs: haec interiōra cum paucīs ex ipsō saepe cognōvimus
phrases.english: but those outward things we often learned from him with many others, these inner ones with few

sources: Lewis & Short: externus · Lewis & Short: exterior · Lewis & Short: exter
